title: Native TUI consumers and historical residuals

rows.operation: The interactive session starts, prints the product header and the startup help/command row, and keeps the visible help readable at the supported widths.
rows.consumer: InteractiveSessionRun -> InteractiveEngine -> InteractiveView; the real terminal path constructs the startup surface before the prompt editor is active.
rows.cppEvidence: Native boot captures (`/tmp/1051-cpp-boot*`) pass. At 72 columns pike renders `! bash ·` at the first-row end and wraps `ctrl+o more`; frozen pi keeps `! bash` together and starts `· ctrl+o more` on the next row. Pike also omits the static logo row and the Pi docs line.
rows.recommendation: Do not treat the 72-column boundary or the missing header rows as accepted. Decide the branding/animation exclusion separately; align the command/help text and preserve the full startup help.

rows.notes: The pi header includes the v1.3.0 version/branding rows; the static logo may fall under the pi branding exclusion, but the help wrap is a behavioral difference.

rows.operation: A run exposes working/busy state, blocks prompt submission or queues it as upstream does, and restores the editor after settlement.
rows.consumer: InteractiveSessionRun event loop -> InteractiveView status/editor; extension contexts observe the same busy state.

scenarios: program status reports idle, blocked, working, done and error through the terminal contract

rows.cppEvidence: The C++ working-status tests pass (`[footer]`, `[cursor]` focused runs). The pi program-status capture shows working/done/error transitions. C++ has no extension `ctx.isIdle()`/busy context; extension busy semantics are tracked in #1049.

rows.cppEvidence: The pi capture observes: factory theme keys `borderColor,selectList`, KeybindingsManager, 16 copied action handlers, text `before-install` transferred, focus true, onSubmit/onChange assigned, padding 0, autocomplete max 5, provider installed; thinking border 108,118,123 -> 104,128,141; Bash border 94,178,134; restore carries `after-install` and focus false; reinstall carries `after-installdefault-typed`; the submitted draft invokes the copied `onSubmit` once and clears the editor; each frame has exactly two editor border rows. C++ `[extension_ui]` passes 321 assertions/17 cases, including text/focus/restore and reload paths. No C++ dual-runtime cell captures the border-token/callback values yet (#1033).
rows.recommendation: Update #1033 with this pi observation; add the Pike-side cell and compare values before closing. Do not claim full dual-runtime verification from the C++ unit tests alone.

rows.operation: Agent tool execution records a monotonic duration that carries through results, events, persistence/resume and the rendered settled tool block; partial calls have no final duration.
rows.consumer: Agent execution -> tool result event -> ToolExecutionComponent render context.

scenarios: runToolCall runs the hooks and reports execute-only duration
tool duration survives the public session record round trip

rows.cppSeam: `src/coding_agent/tui/ToolExecutionComponent.cpp` stamps `system_clock` at render time; `BashRenderer.cpp:duration_line` renders only settled `Took`; there is no `durationMs` field through results/persistence/resume.
rows.cppEvidence: `BashRendererTest` covers exact `Took` shapes from the render clock. The C++ seam does not carry duration through results/events or non-Bash renderers; no fresh v1.3.0 C++ duration cell was captured.
rows.boundary: Agent tool execution -> result/event -> TUI renderer
rows.recommendation: Use a monotonic clock at execute start; carry `durationMs` through the result/event/persistence/render path and exclude hooks. Do not copy model-response timing.

rows.operation: `/thinking` shows the supported levels, marker and help; Enter settles on the selected level.
rows.consumer: InteractiveSessionRun -> ThinkingSelector/InteractiveEngine.
rows.cppEvidence: The captures are not an availability comparison. The C++ fixture uses `tests::make_full_thinking_model("faux-1")`, whose explicit `thinkingLevelMap` maps all seven levels, so `ai::get_supported_thinking_levels` returns `off,minimal,low,medium,high,xhigh,max`. The frozen pi fixture's `faux-1` is `reasoning:true` with no `thinkingLevelMap`; pi `getSupportedThinkingLevels` therefore returns `off,minimal,low,medium,high`. The five common rows, title/help text, `→ ✓ off` marker and descriptions are directly comparable; pi has a blank row between the `>` prompt and first item and C++ does not. The C++ scenario passes its own 27 assertions but does not compare maps or availability.
rows.recommendation: Reuse/update #810 for the matched layout/fixture comparison: add a matched-`thinkingLevelMap` scenario and resolve the evidenced blank-row layout difference. Do not add `xhigh`/`max` from this capture; availability parity is unverified until both harnesses use the same map.
rows.membershipAuthority: ADR 0075 §Selected capability additions — TUI and consumers advances the complete Linux TUI target to v1.3.0, including OSC 7501, cursor behavior, dynamic padding, selection reset, Herdr and overlay/wheel/shifted-key fixes. #1044 selects this Native TUI consumer audit.
rows.notes: Configuration mismatch: C++ fixture maps seven levels; pi fixture omits the map and therefore has five. This is not evidence that C++ omits levels or that pi omits them for a mapped model.

rows.operation: The toolkit formats and sends idle/working/blocked/done/error/clear program status over OSC 7501, gates on terminal support and honors `PI_PROGRAM_STATUS`.
rows.consumer: Terminal contract -> terminal writer; InteractiveMode reporter is the product caller.

scenarios: program status reports idle, blocked, working, done and error through the terminal contract

rows.cppSeam: No C++ equivalent: `src/tui/include/cch/tui/Terminal.hpp` has no `set_program_status`; `ProcessTerminal`/`VirtualTerminal` emit only OSC 9;4 progress.
rows.cppEvidence: The pi capture records the exact calls `idle {app:pi}`, `blocked {kind:question,message:Probe dialog,app:pi}`, `idle`, `working`, `done`, `working`, `error {message:deterministic failure,app:pi}` on our recording terminal. C++ has no protocol or terminal method; this is a missing capability.
rows.recommendation: Implement the protocol in the toolkit, then wire the reporter; verify raw OSC bytes in a real terminal/PTY.
rows.membershipAuthority: ADR 0075 §Selected capability additions — TUI and consumers advances the complete Linux TUI target to v1.3.0, including OSC 7501, cursor behavior, dynamic padding, selection reset, Herdr and overlay/wheel/shifted-key fixes. #1044 selects this Native TUI consumer audit.

rows.operation: InteractiveMode reports working, blocked, done, error and idle from agent/session events and dialog open/close, deduplicating identical statuses.
rows.consumer: InteractiveSessionRun events/dialogs -> ProgramStatusReporter -> Terminal.setProgramStatus.

scenarios: program status reports idle, blocked, working, done and error through the terminal contract

rows.cppSeam: `src/coding_agent/tui/ProgramStatusReporter.{hpp,cpp}` reports working, blocked, done, error and idle to `cch_tui::Terminal::set_program_status`, deduplicating identical statuses; `InteractiveEngine` routes the agent/session events, compaction boundaries and dialog open/close into it.
rows.cppEvidence: The C++ reporter is a port of pi's `program-status-reporter.ts` state machine: the same agent_start/message_end/compaction_start/compaction_end/agent_settled transitions, the same blocked-map 'most recent dialog wins' rule, the same `firstLine` error text with its 'Error' fallback, and the same dedup on the reported status. `tests/coding_agent/tui/ProgramStatusReporterTest.cpp` and `tests/coding_agent/tui/ProgramStatusEvidenceTest.cpp` replay the frozen `fixtures/pi-v1.3.0/audit-1051/program-status.json` states (idle, blocked, idle, working, done, working, error) as literal OSC 7501 wire bytes on a real pseudo-terminal.
rows.recommendation: Implemented by #1123. The reporter is wired into `InteractiveSessionRun`; the remaining work is the ledger's own accepted C++ comparison, which the consolidation pipeline does not write.

rows.capability: /export JSONL: serialize the current session branch as a pi session file
rows.operation: The /export command writes the session header first and then the current branch (getBranch(), root-to-leaf), rewriting every written line's parentId into a linear chain that starts at null, with one trailing newline. The .jsonl destination suffix selects this lane; every other spelling exports HTML.
rows.consumer: InteractiveEngineHost /export dispatch -> cch::harness::transcript_export_handler -> cch::harness::session::SessionStore; the Native TUI slash command is the caller.

scenarios: the exported file is pi's session header followed by the current branch with a null-anchored parent chain

rows.cppSeam: `src/agent/harness/TranscriptExport.cpp` (harness::transcript_export_handler); `src/coding_agent/tui/InteractiveEngineHost.cpp` selects the JSONL lane when the destination ends in `.jsonl`; `tests/coding_agent/session/TranscriptExportTest.cpp` is the regression surface.
rows.cppEvidence: C++ implements pi's rule: the header line comes from EntrySerializer::serialize_header, the branch is store.get_branch() reversed to root-to-leaf, and every written line's parentId is the previous written entry's id starting at null. tests/coding_agent/session/TranscriptExportTest.cpp covers the header, the branch-only scope of a branched tree, the null-anchored parent chain, the one-trailing-newline shape, and that SessionStore::load() accepts the result. These are C++ regression checks only: no frozen pi capture covers the export output, so no value comparison against pi exists.
rows.boundary: The transcript export stays a local file write owned by the application; it is not a share/upload service (see the excluded /share row) and it does not migrate or reinterpret stored user data.
rows.recommendation: Capture the frozen pi v1.3.0 export output for the same session tree and compare the header, the branch-only scope, the parent chain and the trailing newline byte-for-byte before this row can leave unverified. The C++ test proves the C++ contract, not pi parity.

The /export, /import and /share slash commands are pi v1.3.0 application Session capabilities routed by the Native TUI.
rows.notes: No registered artifact scenario names the export output: the audit bundles cover session persistence, toolkit behavior and the Native TUI product differentials, and none of them exercises serializeSessionBranch. The row is therefore unverified, not upstream-captured.

rows.capability: /export HTML: render the session as pi's self-contained HTML document
rows.operation: The /export command writes pi's HTML export by default (a destination not ending in .jsonl), substituting the vendored template.html/css/js and the marked/highlight vendor bundles, injecting the theme variables, and embedding the base64 SESSION_DATA payload in pi's sessionData shape ({header, entries, leafId, systemPrompt?, tools?, renderedTools?}).
rows.consumer: InteractiveEngineHost /export dispatch -> cch::coding_agent::tui::export_session_to_html -> cch::harness::session::SessionStore; the Native TUI slash command is the caller.

scenarios: the exported document has every pi template slot substituted and its SESSION_DATA payload decodes to pi's sessionData shape

rows.cppSeam: `src/coding_agent/tui/HtmlExport.{hpp,cpp}` (generate_session_html, export_session_to_html); the vendored pi template assets live in `third_party/pi-export-html/` (pi is MIT, Copyright 2025 Mario Zechner); `tests/coding_agent/tui/HtmlExportTest.cpp` is the regression surface.
rows.cppEvidence: C++ vendors pi's template assets byte-for-byte and performs pi's exact slot substitution, including JavaScript String.prototype.replace semantics (`$$` collapses to `$`) and the `{{HIGHLIGHT_JS}}` re-expansion artifact inside the vendored highlight.js bundle. tests/coding_agent/tui/HtmlExportTest.cpp proves every named slot is substituted, that the base64 SESSION_DATA payload decodes to pi's member set, and that the theme variables are injected. These are C++ regression checks only: no frozen pi capture covers the emitted document, so no byte comparison against pi's own output exists.
rows.boundary: The HTML export is a local file write owned by the application; it is not a share/upload service and carries no outbound network behavior.
rows.recommendation: Capture the frozen pi v1.3.0 HTML export for the same session and compare the emitted document byte-for-byte before this row can leave unverified. The missing pre-rendered custom-tool HTML recorded as a gap is a real remaining difference and is not covered by the C++ regression.
blockers: C++ emits no renderedTools member: pi's preRenderCustomTools renders custom tool calls and results through pi's TUI renderer pipeline into HTML, while the C++ harness tool renderers produce ANSI text only, so a custom tool's HTML presentation is missing. pi treats the member as optional and falls back to a tool-name header, so the document stays valid, but the rendering differs.

rows.capability: /import: copy a session JSONL file into the session directory and switch to it
rows.operation: The /import command takes one path argument, reports the usage error "Usage: /import <path.jsonl>" when it is absent, asks for a confirmation before any file operation, copies the file into the session directory with pi's -1/-2 collision suffix, opens the imported session, replaces the current session and reports "Session imported from: <path>".
rows.consumer: InteractiveEngineHost /import dispatch -> SessionFlowController::open_import -> cch::coding_agent::tui::{import_path_argument,copy_imported_session} -> the asynchronous Session replacement (Session Assembly); the Native TUI slash command is the caller.

scenarios: a confirmed import copies the file into the session directory and the imported session becomes the current session

rows.cppSeam: `src/coding_agent/tui/SessionImport.{hpp,cpp}` (import_path_argument, import_destination_path, copy_imported_session); `src/coding_agent/tui/SessionFlowControllerImport.cpp` (the confirmation, the copy, the missing-cwd prompt and the session replacement); `src/coding_agent/tui/InteractiveEngineHost.cpp:492` (the dispatch); `tests/coding_agent/tui/SessionImportTest.cpp` and `tests/coding_agent/tui/ImportSlashCommandInteractiveTest.cpp` are the regression surfaces.
rows.cppEvidence: C++ implements pi's rule: the usage error is verbatim, the confirmation precedes every file operation, the destination is the session directory joined with the source base name (or the first free -1, -2, ... variant), the copy never overwrites, the imported session is opened through the ordinary session replacement and becomes the current session, and the status line is pi's wording. tests/coding_agent/tui/SessionImportTest.cpp covers the path-argument spellings, the collision suffix and the exclusive copy; tests/coding_agent/tui/ImportSlashCommandInteractiveTest.cpp drives the VirtualTerminal for the usage error, the accepted import, the declined import, the collision suffix and the missing file. These are C++ regression checks only: no frozen pi capture covers the import flow, so no value comparison against pi exists.
rows.boundary: The import copies one session file into the current session directory and switches the running session; it is not an import/migration/automatic upgrade/dual-read of historical Pike durable data, and no existing user data is deleted or reinterpreted.
rows.recommendation: Capture the frozen pi v1.3.0 import flow for the same source file and compare the confirmation, the destination name, the replacement and the status lines before this row can leave unverified. The two recorded gaps are real and stay open.
blockers: The missing-cwd override path has no /import-specific regression: C++ implements pi's MissingSessionCwdError handling in SessionFlowControllerImport.cpp (the header cwd is read from the copied file, a vanished cwd prompts with pi's 'Session cwd not found' wording and the answer becomes the replacement request's cwd override), but only the /resume path is covered by an interactive test (tests/coding_agent/tui/SessionSelectorInteractiveTest.cpp); the import variant of the same prompt is untested.
C++ has no session_before_switch extension hook: pi's importFromJsonl emits it before the copy and aborts on cancel, while the C++ import path has no such hook to fire.
